title: 3 John
subtitle: The Third Letter of John - Key Notes, Cross-References, and Messianic Connections (WEB)

items.value: Third John is the shortest book in the Bible, just over two hundred words in Greek. It is a personal note to a friend named Gaius, and it is about three men: one who opened his door, one who loved to be first, and one with a good name among everyone.
It is short enough to read in a minute and long enough to find yourself in it.

sections.heading: How this study is put together

items.value: Each of the shortest books in the Bible is one chapter long, so each one is a complete study in a single guide, laid out the same way as every other book in this series.

values: **Key Notes** - observations worth having in hand before you read, each ending with the verses it comes from.
**Key Cross-References** - passages that stand behind or alongside the text, grouped by theme.
**Messianic Connections** - places where the text reaches back into the Hebrew Scriptures or points ahead to the Messiah. Where an entry is a pattern rather than a prediction, the note says so.
**For Further Study** - places to go deeper.
**Introduction** - the book read as a whole before you read it in parts.
**The text itself**, printed in full in the World English Bible, with footnote markers on the verses the references belong to.

items.value: Every scripture reference is a live link to the World English Bible on BibleGateway. In the app, tapping a footnote marker shows the full text of the passages cited and a line on why they connect.

sections.heading: A note on the divine names

items.value: In the notes and introductions this study uses **Yahweh** for the covenant name of God and **Yahshua** for the Messiah. The printed scripture text is never altered; the World English Bible stands exactly as the translators set it, so our own speech and the translator's work stay visibly distinct.
The writer calls himself the elder, as in 2 John. Early tradition identifies him as the apostle John in old age.

values: **Verses 1-4** - a prayer for Gaius, and no greater joy than children walking in truth.
**Verses 5-8** - hospitality to traveling brothers who went out for the sake of the Name.
**Verses 9-10** - Diotrephes, who loves to be first.
**Verses 13-14** - face to face, and greet the friends by name.

chapters.heading: 3 JOHN - Walking in Truth, a Man Who Loved to Be First, and Greet the Friends by Name
chapters.title: Walking in Truth, a Man Who Loved to Be First, and Greet the Friends by Name
keyNotes: 3 John is the shortest book in the Bible by word count, just over two hundred words in Greek. It would have fit on a single sheet of papyrus (3 John 1:1-14).
Gaius was a common name; there are several in the New Testament. This one is known only from this letter, and the elder calls him beloved four times (3 John 1:1, 1:2, 1:5, 1:11).

"I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers." This was a normal way to open a letter in that world - I hope you are well. It is a prayer for a friend, not a promise that faith guarantees wealth (3 John 1:2).

Notice the measure, though: even as your soul prospers. John wants Gaius's outward life to be as healthy as his inner life already is. Few of us would want that prayer prayed over us honestly (3 John 1:2).
Prosperity in Scripture is tied to the word: meditate on this book of the instructions day and night, and then you will make your way prosperous (3 John 1:2, Joshua 1:8, Psalm 1:3).
"Your truth, even as you walk in truth." Truth here is not only what Gaius believes. It is how he walks (3 John 1:3, Psalm 26:3).

"I have no greater joy than this, to hear about my children walking in truth." The elder's spiritual children, those who came to faith through him. Proverbs: the father of the righteous has great joy (3 John 1:4, Proverbs 23:24).

"For those who are brothers and strangers." Gaius welcomed traveling believers he had never met. The Torah commanded it: love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in Egypt (3 John 1:5, Deuteronomy 10:19).
Abraham ran out to meet three strangers, washed their feet and fed them, and found he was entertaining messengers of Yahweh (3 John 1:5, Genesis 18:2-5, Hebrews 13:2).
"Send them forward on their journey in a way worthy of God." To send forward meant to supply them with what they needed for the next stage - food, money, sometimes a companion (3 John 1:6).
"For the sake of the Name they went out." Just the Name - no need to say whose. Malachi: from the rising of the sun my name is great among the nations (3 John 1:7, Malachi 1:11).
"Taking nothing from the Gentiles." They would not accept support from the unbelievers they were reaching, so that no one could say they were selling the message (3 John 1:7).

"That we may be fellow workers for the truth." The one who houses the messenger shares in the message. It is the reverse of 2 John, where welcoming a deceiver made you a partner in his evil (3 John 1:8, 2 John 1:11).

"Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them." One Greek word: he loves first place. Pride, named in a single word. Moses, by contrast, was more humble than any man on the earth (3 John 1:9, Numbers 12:3).
Diotrephes would not receive the elder's letter. He did not argue doctrine. The problem the letter names is not what he believed but what he loved - being first (3 John 1:9).

Four charges against him: he slanders the elder with wicked words, refuses the brothers, forbids others to receive them, and throws out of the assembly those who do. Pride always ends up putting people out (3 John 1:10).
"If I come, I will call attention to his deeds." The elder does not gossip about him in the dark. He promises to address it openly, in person (3 John 1:10).
"Don't imitate that which is evil, but that which is good." People become like whoever they watch. The psalm: depart from evil, and do good (3 John 1:11, Psalm 34:14).
"He who does evil hasn't seen God." Not has not heard about God - has not seen Him. Seeing God changes how a person treats people (3 John 1:11).
Demetrius has the testimony of all, of the truth itself, and of the elder. Three witnesses, as the Torah requires. He may have carried the letter (3 John 1:12, Deuteronomy 19:15).
"I am unwilling to write to you with ink and pen." Almost the same words that close 2 John. The elder would rather sit across the table (3 John 1:13, 2 John 1:12).
"We will speak face to face" - again literally mouth to mouth, as Yahweh spoke with Moses (3 John 1:14, Numbers 12:8).
"Peace be to you" is shalom, the greeting the risen Lord gave in the locked room (3 John 1:14, John 20:19).
"Greet the friends by name." Not the brothers, here - the friends. And by name. The good shepherd calls his own sheep by name (3 John 1:14, John 10:3).

intro: Third John, the shortest book in the Bible at just over two hundred Greek words, is a personal note from the elder to his friend Gaius, and it turns on three men. It opens with a prayer that Gaius may prosper and be in health as his soul prospers - an ordinary letter-writer's greeting, not a promise of wealth, though its measure is searching: that his outward life might match the health of his inner life. The elder has no greater joy than to hear that his children are walking in the truth.

Gaius has been welcoming traveling brothers he had never met and sending them on their way well supplied, as the Torah commands love for the stranger and as Abraham welcomed three visitors and found he was entertaining Yahweh's messengers. They had gone out for the sake of the Name, taking nothing from the Gentiles, and those who support them become fellow workers for the truth.

Diotrephes is described in a single word: he loves to be first. No false doctrine is charged against him, only pride, and the pride runs its usual course - rejecting the elder's letter, slandering him, refusing the brothers, forbidding others to receive them, and expelling those who do. The elder promises to address it openly when he comes, and urges Gaius not to imitate what is evil but what is good, since whoever does evil has not seen God. Demetrius is commended by everyone, by the truth itself and by the elder - three witnesses. The elder lays down his pen, preferring to speak face to face, and closes with peace and a request to greet the friends by name, as the Good Shepherd calls His own.

verses.1: The elder to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.
verses.2: Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers.
verses.3: For I rejoiced greatly, when brothers came and testified about your truth, even as you walk in truth.
verses.4: I have no greater joy than this, to hear about my children walking in truth.
verses.5: Beloved, you do a faithful work in whatever you accomplish for those who are brothers and strangers.
verses.6: They have testified about your love before the assembly. You will do well to send them forward on their journey in a way worthy of God,
verses.7: because for the sake of the Name they went out, taking nothing from the Gentiles.
verses.8: We therefore ought to receive such, that we may be fellow workers for the truth.
verses.9: I wrote to the assembly, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, doesn’t accept what we say.
verses.10: Therefore if I come, I will call attention to his deeds which he does, unjustly accusing us with wicked words. Not content with this, neither does he himself receive the brothers, and those who would, he forbids and throws out of the assembly.
verses.11: Beloved, don’t imitate that which is evil, but that which is good. He who does good is of God. He who does evil hasn’t seen God.
verses.12: Demetrius has the testimony of all, and of the truth itself; yes, we also testify, and you know that our testimony is true.
verses.13: I had many things to write to you, but I am unwilling to write to you with ink and pen;
verses.14: but I hope to see you soon, and we will speak face to face. Peace be to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.

cites.text: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.

2.why: meditate on the book of the instructions day and night and you will make your way prosperous, and whatever he does shall prosper

cites.text: For your loving kindness is before my eyes. I have walked in your truth.

Then Yahweh may establish his word which he spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If your children are careful of their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail you,’ he said, ‘a man on the throne of Israel.’

3.why: I have walked in your truth, and children who walk before me in truth with all their heart

cites.text: The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him. Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!
The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father; but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.

4.why: the father of the righteous has great joy, and a wise son makes a glad father

cites.text: Therefore love the foreigner; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood opposite him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth, and said, “My lord, if now I have found favor in your sight, please don’t go away from your servant. Now let a little water be fetched, wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree. I will get a morsel of bread so you can refresh your heart. After that you may go your way, now that you have come to your servant.” They said, “Very well, do as you have said.”

5.why: love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in Egypt, and Abraham running to welcome three strangers

cites.text: For from the rising of the sun even to the going down of the same, my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense will be offered to my name, and a pure offering: for my name is great among the nations,” says Yahweh of Armies.
They therefore departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for Jesus’ name.

7.why: my name is great among the nations, and rejoicing to suffer dishonor for the Name

cites.text: From the rising of the sun to the going down of the same, Yahweh’s name is to be praised.

God said moreover to Moses, “You shall tell the children of Israel this, ‘Yahweh, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.

7.why: from the rising of the sun Yahweh's name is to be praised, and this is my name forever

cites.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”

8.why: how beautiful are the feet of him who brings good news and publishes peace

cites.text: Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the men who were on the surface of the earth.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

9.why: Moses more humble than all the men on the earth, and pride goes before destruction

cites.text: Depart from evil, and do good. seek peace, and pursue it.
Depart from evil, and do good. Live securely forever.

11.why: depart from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it

cites.text: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall a matter be established.

12.why: every matter established at the mouth of two or three witnesses

cites.text: With him, I will speak mouth to mouth, even plainly, and not in riddles; and he shall see Yahweh’s form. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?”
As for me, I shall see your face in righteousness. I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with seeing your form.

14.why: with Moses I speak mouth to mouth, and I shall be satisfied seeing your form

cites.text: For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’

14.why: the Prince of Peace, and Yahweh lift up his face toward you and give you peace

cites.text: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out.

Moses said to Yahweh, “Behold, you tell me, ‘Bring up this people:’ and you haven’t let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’

14.why: the shepherd calls his own sheep by name, and I know you by name
